verdicts.reason: Opened fmtWhen (lines 56-64): it calls new Date(ev.startDate) and new Date(ev.endDate) on date-only strings, which JavaScript reads as midnight UTC. Reproduced in Node: with TZ=America/Chicago and TZ=America/Los_Angeles the stored pair 2026-09-23 / 2026-09-24 prints 'Sep 22 – Sep 23'; UTC, Berlin and Tokyo print 'Sep 23 – Sep 24'. The two older screens append T00:00:00 (ds/components/EventListDS.tsx:29, components/EventRow.tsx:19) and print the right day, so only the default screen is wrong. Severity 3 stands: every date on the default screen is one day early for a user in the Americas. The fix is correct and minimal: parsing `${iso.slice(0, 10)}T12:00:00` printed 'Sep 23 – Sep 24' in all five time zones I ran, and it is the same form get-there.ts:97 and the Briefing (src/briefing/v4/lib/world-events.ts:25) already use. Setting process.env.TZ inside a test has a precedent in this repository (tests/ae-invariants.test.js:50-60) and works because vitest runs test files in forked processes.
verdicts.checked: src/outdoors-events/v4/OutdoorsEventsV4.tsx:56-64; Node run under five TZ values

verdicts.reason: Line 59 formats with month and day only. Both demo books list RecFest USA first as 'Sep 23 – Sep 24' (stored 2026-09-23/24, already over on 2026-11-17) above rows dated April and May 2027 (corpus-smb/outdoors-events.txt lines 9, 19, 30), so the reader has to work out which year each row means and nothing says the first event is finished. This also happens in real use: events are never removed when they end, and a search made in the autumn returns events in the following year. The Briefing already treats ended events differently (world-events.ts:44-50 leaves them out). The proposed change is accurate and small: the year only when it differs from the current year, and the one word 'ended' when the last day is before today. The date column is 92px wide (outdoors-events-v4.css:34) and already wraps, so the longer text fits on a second line. When implementing, compare calendar-day strings (last day < today's YYYY-MM-DD) as the Briefing does, and use the local-day parser from OE-001, so the two pages agree on which events are over.

Lines 142-143 print run.status unchanged, so the page shows the stored keys 'completed', 'throttled', 'failed' or 'running'; an empty completed_at prints 'just now' whatever the row's age; and the count has no singular ('1 events returned'). The previous screen maps the same keys to labels (ds/lib/adapters.ts:24-30). All three parts are real. 'Throttled' matches the code as the reviewer describes it: from $1.00 spent in the previous 7 days the prompt asks for direct-tier events only and allows 3 searches instead of 6 (index.ts:36, 128-131, 166, 204; probe output confirmed). Two corrections to the fix. (1) A reduced-budget search is inserted with status 'throttled' before the model call (index.ts:179), so a row that never closed can carry that status with no completed_at; choosing the sentence by status alone would call it a finished search. Test completed_at first. (2) Build each sentence as one validated template with .replace(), the pattern src/lib/voice/t.ts:17-21 prescribes, instead of joining fragments such as t("The search on") + date + t("did not finish").
verdicts.finalProposed:
Replace lines 142-143 with a formatter (never print run.status):
const date = new Date(run.completedAt ?? run.startedAt).toLocaleDateString();
const count = run.eventsWritten === 1 ? t("1 event returned") : t("{n} events returned").replace("{n}", String(run.eventsWritten));
- completed_at empty (any status): t("A search started on {date} has not finished.", { class: "body" }).replace("{date}", date)
- status failed: t("The search on {date} did not finish.", { class: "body" }).replace("{date}", date), followed by ` · ${count}` only when eventsWritten > 0
- status throttled: `${t("Last search")} ${date} · ${count} · ${t("limited to directly relevant events to stay within the 7-day search budget", { class: "body" })}`
- otherwise (completed): `${t("Last search")} ${date} · ${count}`
Add a render test for the four cases plus a 'throttled' row with no completed_at.

verdicts.reason: Line 103 labels the × 'Dismiss' and calls removeEvent, which deletes the row (state.ts:181-191, lib/persistence.ts:165-177). The search matches an existing row only by dedupe_key (index.ts:313-324), so once the row is gone the same event is inserted again as 'Watching'. Reproduced with the real handler and stand-ins: run, delete the row, run again → the event is back with status 'watching'. No status hides a row on any of the three screens, so the user has no way to keep an unwanted event out of the list. A control named 'Dismiss' whose result is undone by the next search is a real mismatch between label and behavior. The label change ('Delete event' as title and aria-label) says what the control does today and matches the 'Delete' button on the two older screens. Making a dismissal last (× sets 'archived', archived rows leave the three groups, real delete only for manually added rows) changes behavior and the settled layout, so sending that part to the owner is right; it is also the only way the area can do what canon §4.22 says the user can do ('marks, prioritizes, dismisses').

changeStatus and removeEvent do nothing when the request fails (state.ts:170-175, 184-187): no message is set, and no test covers either function. The failure is silent on all three screens. One correction to the description: the status control keeps showing the unsaved value only on the default screen. Its row reads neither busyRowId nor any other signal that changes, so it is not re-rendered. On the two older screens the row reads busyRowId (ds/components/EventListDS.tsx:44, components/EventRow.tsx:40), which changes twice during the call; Preact re-applies value={event.status} whenever it differs from the element's value (preact 10.29 diff/index.js:570-582), so there the control returns to the saved status, still with no explanation. The fix works on all three: a row that reads a rowError signal is re-rendered when it is set, which also puts the default screen's control back. The two messages match the wording of the existing save error ('Couldn't save the event. Check the connection and try again.', state.ts:153).

Checked each control. The status <select> (lines 94-102) has no label, aria-label or title; both walkthroughs record it as '(unlabelled field)' (corpus/outdoors-events.txt:17, corpus-smb/outdoors-events.txt:17). The four links contain one emoji each and a title (lines 85-92), so their accessible name is the emoji and the title is only a description. The delete button's content is '×' (line 103). The two text inputs are named by placeholder alone and the date input has no name (lines 194-199). Neither error <span> has a role (lines 148, 205), while the previous screen's errors use role="alert" (ds/components/DiscoveryConsoleDS.tsx:60). The proposed aria-labels repeat the visible titles, and role="alert" matches the older screens. When applying it, the delete button's accessible name is more useful with the event name in it, as the oldest screen has (`Delete ${event.name}`, components/EventRow.tsx:122), because a row of identical 'Delete event' buttons cannot be told apart in a screen reader's list; the same applies to 'Status'.

Line 47 prints `{w.tempC}°` with no unit. The value is Celsius: the forecast request at get-there.ts:59 has no temperature_unit parameter, and Open-Meteo's default is Celsius. The Briefing asks for Fahrenheit (src/briefing/v4/lib/weather.ts:127, asserted in weather.test.ts:55) and prints `{tempF}°` (BriefingV4.tsx:478). So two default pages of one product show a bare degree figure in different units, and a US seller reads 24° for Las Vegas as cold. The tooltip is also inexact: the request asks for one day (start_date=end_date=day, line 59), and with no date it uses today (line 50). Correction to the fix: showing '°C' is accurate but leaves the two pages in different units. The Briefing's Fahrenheit is recorded as the product's choice (CLAUDE.md session log 2026-07-13: 'one call for current + 7 days, °F'), so use the same unit here and print it. This is one request parameter and one field name used in two files; nothing is stored.
verdicts.finalProposed: get-there.ts:59: add `&temperature_unit=fahrenheit` to the forecast URL; rename WeatherGlance.tempC to tempF (lines 9-10 and 67) and add `readonly today: boolean` set to `!dateIso`. OutdoorsEventsV4.tsx:47: render `{glyph} {w.tempF}°F` with title={w.today ? t("Today's forecast high at this location", { class: "body" }) : t("Forecast high on the event's first day", { class: "body" })}. In the new get-there test, assert the request contains temperature_unit=fahrenheit.

verdicts.reason: calendarIcs uses today's date when startIso is empty (get-there.ts:93) and the end date falls back to today plus one day (lines 97-98). The link is rendered for every row (OutdoorsEventsV4.tsx:92), including a row whose date column reads 'date not set'. Downloading it puts an all-day entry on today's date in the seller's calendar for an event that has no date. An undated row is reachable two ways: the manual form does not require a date, and the search prompt allows start_date null (index.ts:107). Rendering the link only when ev.startDate exists is the smallest correct change; the flights and hotel links already leave the date out when there is none (get-there.ts:78, 84).

The generated VEVENT has SUMMARY, DTSTART, DTEND and an optional LOCATION only (get-there.ts:100-111). RFC 5545 section 3.6.1 lists UID and DTSTAMP as required properties of a VEVENT. The practical effect (a second import of the same file adds a duplicate, and a strict client may refuse the file) was not executed by the reviewer or by me, so severity 1 with medium confidence is right. The two added lines are correct: the DTSTAMP expression produces the form 20261117T010203Z, and a UID built from the start date and the event name is stable across downloads, which is what lets a calendar recognise a repeat import.

'Buyer context' appears at lines 52, 133 and 161 and in the help text (src/lib/operator-help/registry.ts:192). It is not Antaeus vocabulary, but it is an abstraction the reader has to unpack, and the current remediation notes show it was the earlier pass's own coinage (docs/language-remediation-2026/13_ADVERSARIAL_PHASE_AUDIT.md:182), not approved text. The help sentence also tells the user to review 'the product category and buyer context used for discovery'; the search is sent product category, what you sell and value proposition only (index.ts:117-126), so there is no buyer context to review. Severity 1 is right. Two corrections to the fix. (1) Header, line 133: the original working set gives an exact replacement for this string, 'events relevant to your target buyers' (10_COPY_IMPLEMENTATION_MANIFEST_BATCH_03.json exact_replacements[16]). It is not contradicted by the code and matches the workspace map ('find events where target buyers may be present', src/lib/ground/motion.ts:40), so use it verbatim; adding 'market and' is not needed and the record then counts as implemented. (2) Group heading, line 52: with that header, 'Relevant to your target buyers' would repeat the page description as the name of one of three groups. Keep the approved noun phrase 'Adjacent events' and drop only the attendance claim the code cannot support ('…YOUR BUYERS ATTEND'). The help-text sentence is fine as proposed.
verdicts.finalProposed: OutdoorsEventsV4.tsx:133: t("events relevant to your target buyers", { class: "body" }). Line 52 label: t("Adjacent events for your target buyers", { class: "body" }), keeping the sub-line 'events focused on the roles, functions, or problems you sell into'. Line 161: see OE-011. src/lib/operator-help/registry.ts:192: "If no useful events are returned, check the product category saved for your workspace, which the search uses, or add a known event manually."

verdicts.reason: Lines 160-161 tell the user to 'Run event discovery', but the only control is the button 'Find relevant events' (line 152). The same text shows whenever the list is empty, including after a search that returned nothing, where it tells the user to repeat what they just did. Minor, as rated. Three corrections to the fix. (1) 'Select Find relevant events to search…' is hard to parse because nothing marks where the button's name ends; say 'the Find relevant events button'. (2) The second variant sends the user to 'check the product category saved for your workspace', which a user on the default screens has no place to do (see OE-012: the only form that saves it is on the previous and oldest ICP Studio screens). Do not give an instruction the screen cannot support. (3) Use the 'returned no events' variant only when the latest search finished (status completed or throttled) with 0 events; a failed search is already reported by the line above (OE-003).
verdicts.finalProposed:
Latest search finished (status completed or throttled) with eventsWritten 0:

{t("The last search returned no events.")}

{t("You can search again later or add an event manually below.", { class: "body" })}

. Every other empty case:

{t("No events are listed.")}

{t("Use the Find relevant events button to search for scheduled events related to your product category, or add an event manually below.", { class: "body" })}

verdicts.reason: Reproduced with the real handler and stand-ins: with product_category null, and with no workspace_profile row at all, run_one makes the model call with the prompt 'Product category: (product category not set)', stores what comes back, and returns ok:true with status completed; the stored event is in the 'direct' group, which the page heads 'Directly relevant to your category'. run_all skips such workspaces (index.ts:354-362) but run_one, the button's path, has no check (lines 151-205). I also confirmed the reach: the only writers of product_category, what_we_sell and value_prop are ICP Studio's profile form on the previous screen (src/icp-studio/ds/components/IcpBuilder.tsx:184-215) and the oldest (src/icp-studio/components/CommercialProfileBanner.tsx); the default ICP Studio screen has no such field, onboarding writes only its own two columns (src/onboarding/lib/cloud.ts:17-21), and Settings' category is a browser key (src/settings/lib/storage.ts:20). So a workspace set up on the default screens always searches with no input. Severity 3 stands. The guard and the message are right, and the place where a default-screen user enters what they sell is correctly left to the owner. One addition: with the proposed check a workspace that saved only 'what you sell' still passes, and buildUserPrompt would still send the literal line 'Product category: (product category not set)'. Leave that line out when the category is empty.
verdicts.finalProposed: index.ts, in runForWorkspace right after readProfile (line 174) and before the ledger insert: `if (![profile.product_category, profile.what_we_sell, profile.value_prop].some((v) => v?.trim())) return { workspaceId, status: "failed", eventsWritten: 0, cost: 0, searchCount: 0, error: "missing_product_category" };` (no ledger row, no model call). In buildUserPrompt (lines 118-124) push `Product category: ${category}` only when profile.product_category has text. src/outdoors-events/lib/discovery.ts: add `noCategory: "Event search needs a description of what you sell, and none is saved for this workspace. You can still add events manually."` to DISCOVERY_MESSAGES and return it when the response's error is "missing_product_category", before the generic failed message. Tests: a handler case (all three fields empty → ok:false, no ledger row, no model call), a handler case (only what_we_sell set → the prompt has no 'not set' line), and a client case for the new message. OWNER DECISION (unchanged): where a user on the default screens enters what they sell — add the three profile fields to the default ICP Studio screen and name that place in the message, or let the search fall back to the saved ICP.

verdicts.reason: listOutdoorsEvents returns [] for every failure (lib/persistence.ts:105-108); bootEvents and runDiscoveryNow hand that to setEvents, which also sets loaded (state.ts:88-91, 110-112, 134). The default screen then renders its empty state, 'No events found yet. Run event discovery…' (OutdoorsEventsV4.tsx:158-162), so a failed read is shown as a workspace with no events and the user is pointed at a paid search; after a successful search whose reload fails, the list on screen is replaced by the empty state. loadLatestRun likewise returns null on failure (lib/discovery.ts:78-81) and the page then states 'No event search has been run yet.' listOutdoorsEvents has one caller (state.ts), so the change is contained. Two corrections to the fix. (1) tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts:852-878 opens the oldest screen with no database and asserts `.oe-list` is attached; with the change that run lands in the load-failure state, so that state must keep the `.oe-list` class there. (2) src/outdoors-events/lib/discovery.test.ts:91-94 asserts that loadLatestRun returns null on failure; changing it to return undefined would mean rewriting that assertion. Keep the tested contract and add a variant that also reports whether the read succeeded.
verdicts.finalProposed: lib/persistence.ts: listOutdoorsEvents returns null on failure (`Promise<ReadonlyArray<OutdoorsEvent> | null>`). state.ts: `export const loadError: Signal<boolean> = signal(false);`; bootEvents: `const rows = await listOutdoorsEvents(); loadError.value = rows === null; setEvents(rows ?? []);`; in runDiscoveryNow keep the list on screen when the reload returns null. On each screen, before the empty state, when loadError is true render heading t("Your events couldn't be loaded.") and t("Check your connection and reload the page. Your saved events have not been changed.", { class: "body" }) in a role="alert" element: default screen `<div class="oe4-empty" role="alert">`; previous screen a Card with the same two strings; oldest screen `<section class="oe-list oe-list--error" role="alert">` so `.oe-list` is still attached for tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts:874. Last-search line: leave loadLatestRun as tested (null on failure) and add `loadLatestRunResult(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; run: DiscoveryRun | null }>` beside it (loadLatestRun returns its `run`); state stores `latestRunKnown: Signal<boolean>` from `ok`, and the screens print no last-search sentence while it is false. Add state tests for the failed-load path (mock ./lib/persistence and ./lib/discovery).

verdicts.reason: Both walkthroughs show 'No event search has been run yet.' on line 4 and, directly below, events grouped under the three relevance headings with 'View source →' (corpus/outdoors-events.txt:4-35, corpus-smb/outdoors-events.txt:4-32). The seed writes only the events key (js/demo-seed-runtime.js:291-294); every seeded row is marked source_kind:'discovery_run' (js/demo-seed-data-ent.js:690-694, js/demo-seed-data-smb.js:491-494); and the line reads the runs table through the demo data client, whose key 'gtmos_demo__outdoors_events_runs' is never written (src/lib/data-client-demo-local.ts:73-75; grep finds no writer). So the sample states that no search has run while showing a search's results. Seeding one finished run per book fixes it at the source: d() is the seed files' own relative-date helper (js/demo-seed-data-ent.js:18), the demo client reads any array stored under that key, and nothing else reads it. With OE-003 applied the line reads 'Last search {date} · 5 events returned'.

The default row renders date, name, place, weather, relevance sentence and source link (lines 70-80) and never reads ev.notes, ev.kind or ev.tags; the manual form has three inputs (lines 194-199). The previous screen's form has nine fields and its cards show the note (ds/components/EventComposerDS.tsx:52-124, ds/components/EventListDS.tsx:60). The search function is written to leave notes alone on a refresh (index.ts:302-312, test at discovery-function.test.ts:123-131), and the capability map lists notes among the user's own decisions about an event, so on the default screen a protected field can be neither written nor read; both demo books seed notes that never appear. Showing a saved note with the label 'Your note:' is small, accurate, and keeps the seller's words apart from the search's sentence (the same label OE-038 proposes for the older screens). Adding end date, link and note inputs changes the settled default layout, so leaving that to the owner is right.

Line 138 reads 'Search current event sources, then decide which events are worth pursuing.' 'Current event sources' does not say what is searched and can be read as current-event (news) sources; the function runs web searches (anthropic.ts:93-99). Minor, as rated. Correction to the fix: the original working set gives an exact replacement for this slot, 'Antaeus identifies relevant events; you decide which ones are worth pursuing.' (10_COPY_IMPLEMENTATION_MANIFEST_BATCH_03.json exact_replacements[17]; 09_REWRITE_BATCH_03_EXECUTION_AND_UTILITY.md row 26). It is accurate to current behavior (the search finds the events when the user starts it; the user sets a status on the ones worth pursuing), it is not superseded by any owner decision, and the same button sat beside it when it was approved. Use it verbatim instead of a third wording; the record then counts as implemented. The busy label 'Searching the web for events…' is accurate and fine.
verdicts.finalProposed: Line 138: t("Antaeus identifies relevant events; you decide which ones are worth pursuing.", { class: "body" }). Line 152 busy label: t("Searching the web for events…").

verdicts.reason: STATUS_LABEL.passed is 'Passed' (lib/types.ts:65) and is shown in the status list on all three screens. On a list of dated events, some of which are already over, the word reads either as 'we passed on this' or 'this event's date has passed'. The code means the first: the Briefing leaves 'passed' and 'archived' events out of its upcoming list (src/briefing/v4/lib/world-events.ts:60) and the capability map calls the decision 'skipping'. 'Not attending' is unambiguous, sits naturally beside 'Attending' and 'Attended', and changes only the label; the stored key 'passed' and the table's check constraint are untouched. No test pins the word.
verdicts.checked: src/outdoors-events/lib/types.ts:60-67; src/briefing/v4/lib/world-events.ts:60; grep for 'Passed' in tests

verdicts.reason: The prompt's field description allows 'Online' as a place (index.ts:106), and the row shows 'Check flights' and 'Hotels nearby' and runs the weather lookup for any non-empty place (OutdoorsEventsV4.tsx:83-88, 119), so an online event gets a flight search for 'flights to Online'. Real, minor. The guard on the screen is right and should stay whatever the search does, because a manually added event may be online by design (the table comment gives 'Online' as an example place, supabase/migrations/20260601200000_outdoors_events.sql:30). Correction: the prompt change does not need a new owner decision. Canon §4.22 ('finds offline gatherings'), the function README (line 5) and the function's own header (index.ts:4) already say the search is for offline events; the prompt is the one place that disagrees.
verdicts.finalProposed: OutdoorsEventsV4.tsx: add `const isOnline = (w: string | null): boolean => !!w && /^(online|virtual|remote)\b/i.test(w.trim());` and use `ev.whereAt && !isOnline(ev.whereAt)` at line 83 (travel links) and line 119 (weather lookup). index.ts:91: 'Find real, currently scheduled in-person conferences, trade shows, summits, mixers, meetups, and similar events…'; index.ts:106: `"where_at": "string (city and venue)"`; in parseDiscoveredEvents (_shared.ts) skip an event whose where_at matches the same online pattern. Add a parser case for an event with where_at 'Online'.
